- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +3+ points in 3-5 days), model often overshoots in next 5-10 days; apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5 points.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20) and price is trending up, model may underreact; adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.8 points to align with sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizons; if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0 points.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days); cap forecast at 1.2–1.5σ above 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.10) and price is flat, model tends to drift upward; apply slight downward bias (–0.2 to –0.5) to avoid false momentum.
